heroHeadline: BC's Bald Range Fire Declared Under Control as TNRD Downgrades Last Pear Lake-Area Evacuation Orders to Alerts
heroSubtitle: British Columbia's wildfire situation continued to ease as fall weather approaches: the Bald Range fire near Summerland was classified 'under control' (as of Aug 31) with recovery measures now underway for the ~150 destroyed structures, while the Thompson-Nicola and Squamish-Lillooet regional districts downgraded their last remaining Pear Lake-area evacuation orders to alerts on September 3 — though two First Nations, Whispering Pines/Clinton Indian Band and Stswecem'c Xget'tem, still maintain their own evacuation orders. BC's active fire count fell to 150 with under 10% classified out of control, down from 45% the prior week, and the Matthew Creek fire near Kimberley had its area restriction zone reduced as activity eased. In Northwestern Ontario, a handful of small new starts near Nipigon — including one 0.2-hectare fire near Long Lake 58 First Nation — kept the region's active count near 62, with the Rinker Lake Complex (Thunder Bay 36, Dryden 34, Dryden 35 — 377,240 hectares combined) still not under control amid otherwise low activity. The Northwest Territories held steady at 288 fires and 1,694,001 hectares as of September 6. No new deaths were identified this cycle.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
